title: An Efficient White-box LLM Watermarking for IP Protection on Online Market Platforms

problem.claim: Online market platforms need efficient watermarking to protect the intellectual property of shared and deployed LLMs from unauthorized use and duplication.

gap.claim: Existing watermarking techniques are tailored to specific model types, while traditional approaches require substantial data and costly hardware.

contributions.claim: ELLMark is a white-box LLM watermarking technique that embeds watermarks by modifying model weights.
ELLMark filters weights using activation-magnitude correlations and downstream tasks, then applies minimal modification through histogram modulation to preserve performance.
ELLMark provides training-free watermarking with low hardware-resource requirements for online platforms.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on LLaMA-3, OPT, and Phi-3 report 100% watermark-detection success while preserving model performance.
For models with 80B parameters, preprocessing, encoding, and decoding reportedly take less than 7 minutes, 12 minutes, and 18 seconds, respectively.
The method reportedly remains robust against parameter overwriting, re-watermarking, forging, fine-tuning, and pruning attacks.

narrative_sequence.summary: Online market platforms support sharing and deployment of AI models, creating an IP-protection need.
Existing watermarking methods are model-specific and resource-intensive.
ELLMark modifies model weights using filtered correlations and minimal histogram modulation without training.
The authors evaluate ELLMark on three LLM families and report detection, performance, efficiency, and attack-robustness results.

source_observation.claim: The method selects weights using activation magnitudes and downstream-task correlations before applying minimal histogram-based modifications.

interpretation.claim: Targeted, minimal parameter changes may help balance watermark insertion with preservation of model behavior.

application.claim: For model-integrated protection mechanisms, consider selecting parameters by behavioral relevance and minimizing the intervention magnitude.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this tradeoff holds across tasks, architectures, watermark payloads, or attack settings beyond those evaluated.

unknowns: Datasets, downstream tasks, baselines, and evaluation metrics are not specified.
The watermark construction, detection protocol, and attack configurations are not described.
The abstract does not provide independent verification of the reported results.
